title: gustar with le / les, interesar, parecer, me parece bien, ponerle sal

cards.title: Start with the verb: nos gusta
cards.body: It is pleasing (gusta) to us (nos), so not 'nos gustamos'.

cards.title: gustar = to be pleasing TO
cards.body: Store it with 'to', because it takes le / les (to him/her/them), not lo / la.

cards.title: interesar = to be interesting to
cards.body: Interesante is the adjective; interesar (ending in -ar) is a verb. It works like gustar.

examples.en: Is she interested in going out dancing tonight?
examples.es: ¿Le interesa salir a bailar esta noche?

cards.title: parecer = to seem (to)
cards.body: Check the verb type first: parecer is -er, so me parece. Que = that (and qué = what, just as English that → what with a w).

examples.en: It seems to me (that) he doesn't want to go out tonight.
examples.es: Me parece que no quiere salir esta noche.

examples.en: It seems to me he doesn't like it.
examples.es: Me parece que no le gusta.

cards.title: me parece bien = sounds good to me
cards.body: Spanish uses bien (well) where English might say 'good'. You'll pick up the bueno / bien grey area by listening.

examples.en: Doesn't it seem OK to you (formal)?
I'd be interested in seeing it.

cards.title: poner; 'on it' = le
cards.body: 'Put salt on it' = 'put it salt', with le (to/on it).

examples.en: I want to put it here.
I'd like to put a little more salt on it.
examples.es: Me gustaría ponerle un poco más (de) sal.
Me gustaría ponerles un poco más (de) sal.

practice.en: It seems to me he doesn't want to go out tonight.
